pathway.title: Silgan Holdings Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business supports the debt through contract-backed, cost-pass-through earnings rather than growth. Reported EBITDA margins stayed between 13.51% and 14.34% from 2023 to 2025 even though EBITDA fell 7.88% in 2024; about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year contracts that pass metal cost through, while resin cost passes through with a lag. The price is thin metal margins, an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% in 2025, and one concentration, Nestlé at 14% of 2025 net sales under agreements that run through 2032. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17, 21–25, 66–68; calculation D1; calculation D2

Free cash flow covers distributions but has not reduced debt. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was about USD 423 million in 2025, 46.10% of reported EBITDA, and covered dividends and buybacks 2.63 times; yet net debt fell only USD 47.81 million and total debt rose, so the improvement in leverage came from EBITDA growth, not repayment. Free cash flow after shareholder returns was about USD 262 million, a pace that would not shrink net debt quickly against a seasonal swing of the size seen in 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104; calculation D3; calculation D4; calculation D5

Leverage is elevated at the seasonal peak and the 2026 earnings trend does not help. Net debt over reported EBITDA was 3.56x at year-end 2025, and the pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement on that figure is not established; it was 4.67x at September 30, 2026 on last-twelve-months EBITDA, with total debt at 5.03x. Last-twelve-months EBITDA of about USD 904 million is 1.44% below 2025, and it would be a further 3.76% lower, with net leverage at 4.85x, without the USD 34.0 million inventory benefit. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15, 18–20; calculation D2; calculation D6; calculation D10

Liquidity is adequate in aggregate but thinnest in early summer, and two maturity years concentrate the refinancing test. Cash plus revolver availability was about USD 991 million at September 30, 2026 but about USD 754 million at June 30, when revolver availability of USD 402.4 million was below the USD 600 million seasonal need; the USD 1,500.0 million revolver matures in November 2029. At December 31, 2025, 31.89% of principal fell due in 2028 and 28.25% in 2030, together 60.14%. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73, 114; calculation D7; calculation D9

The October 2026 transaction is the swing factor for claim priority and leverage, and the filings do not let a creditor size it. The USD 2.3 billion distribution equals 50.42% of total debt principal at September 30, 2026, 124.37% of the unsecured senior notes and 87.66% of Credit Agreement debt, so which instruments are retired decides whether the remaining parent claims are mostly secured bank debt or mostly unsecured notes; the partnership's USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans rank on its own assets only, and the Trivium acquisition is expected to close in mid-2027, ahead of the 2028 note maturities. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D12

Funding that does not show as debt deepens reliance on banks. Supplier invoices in the supply chain finance program were USD 482.0 million at September 30, 2026, up 24.94% in a year and equal to 10.60% of total debt, and customer programs covered about 16% of net sales; the bank can end the supplier program on short notice, which would turn payables into revolver draws at the point of seasonal peak. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 27–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D13

Financial policy and governance are a moderate risk rather than a decisive one. Dividends took 29.74% of 2025 net income and the USD 500.0 million buyback authorization was unused in the first nine months of 2026, but management states that it uses leverage to fund growth and shareholder returns, interest and other debt expense absorbed 31.7% of 2025 income before interest and taxes, and ownership detail sits in documents that are not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D14

rows.label: Income before interest and income taxes (EBIT)

runs.text: The first strength is contract-backed earnings. About 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year supply arrangements that pass metal cost through, and a majority of dispensing and custom container sales do too, so reported EBITDA margins held between 13.51% and 14.34% across 2023 to 2025. That gives creditors earnings that bend rather than break when input costs move, with resin cost recovery lagging as the exception. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17, 21–22, 58–59; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

The second strength is cash conversion. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was about USD 423 million in 2025, 46.10% of reported EBITDA, which covered dividends and buybacks 2.63 times and left about USD 262 million to reduce debt or fund acquisitions. Operating cash flow is struck after cash interest of about USD 185 million, so that free cash flow is cash left after servicing the debt. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D3; calculation D4

The third strength is a record of early and orderly refinancing. The Credit Agreement was extended to November 2029 for the revolver and November 2030 for term loans in November 2024, EUR 600.0 million of notes were sold at par in September 2025, and the USD 500.0 million secured notes were repaid in March 2026 ahead of their April maturity; no waiver, exchange offer or covenant breach appears in the filings. That lowers the risk that a market window decides the outcome. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71, 119–120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fourth strength is delivery on cost. The USD 50 million cost program was completed, with about USD 20 million of savings in 2024 and about USD 30 million in 2025, which supported the rise in 2025 adjusted EBIT to USD 723.3 million from USD 658.2 million and gives management a lever if volumes soften. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 66

The fifth strength is a conventional governance and audit record, with unqualified opinions, effective internal control and a payout of 29.74% of 2025 net income, which keeps shareholder claims on cash moderate. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D14

The first weakness is that the October 2026 transaction leaves claim priority, perimeter and leverage open. The largest segment by sales would sit in a partnership that is 40% owned by an outside investor and financed by USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans on its own assets, and the effect on consolidated net debt and net leverage is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second weakness is elevated and seasonal leverage with flat 2026 earnings. Net debt over reported EBITDA reached 4.67x at September 30, 2026 against 3.56x at year-end 2025, for which the pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement is not established, unit volumes fell in all segments over the nine months, and adjusted EBIT was flat only because currency, mix in custom containers, manufacturing efficiencies and an inventory benefit offset lower volumes and a less favorable mix elsewhere. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15, 18–20; calculation D6

The third weakness is a concentrated maturity profile. At December 31, 2025, 31.89% of principal fell due in 2028 and 28.25% in 2030, so two refinancing windows carry most of the principal. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D9

The fourth weakness is thin metal margins and one large customer. Metal Containers earned an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% and Nestlé was 14% of net sales, so a small cost lag or a repricing moves group earnings. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 66–68; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fifth weakness is reliance on bank-run funding. Supplier finance invoices of USD 482.0 million and customer receivable programs covering about 16% of net sales move cash forward, and the seasonal borrowing that follows is carried on one revolver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 74; calculation D13

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On October 19, 2026 Silgan announced agreements to create a partnership, Silgan MCC, with an investment vehicle affiliated with funds managed by American Industrial Partners. Silgan would contribute its Metal Containers segment and its food and beverage flat cap closures business and would receive about USD 2.3 billion of cash, which it intends to use to retire certain existing debt, and a 60% controlling ownership interest; the investment vehicle would contribute about USD 1.0 billion of cash for 40%. The partnership would have an independent balance sheet that is fully consolidated into Silgan's statements and would be financed by about USD 4.9 billion of new senior secured term loans and a new senior secured revolving facility of USD 1.0 billion, which the company describes as fully committed and secured by assets of the partnership only. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16

The partnership would also acquire Trivium Packaging B.V., a Netherlands supplier of metal packaging, for a cash payment of about USD 327.5 million and the assumption of about USD 3.1 billion of Trivium's debt. Trivium is one of the competitors that the 2025 annual report names among the most significant in metal containers. Closing is expected in mid-2027 and is subject to regulatory approvals, works council consultation and customary conditions. Costs attributed to announced acquisitions were USD 10.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, against USD 1.1 million in the first nine months of 2025, and adjusted EBIT excludes them; the filing does not tie them to a named transaction. The note gives no agreement terms, no sources and uses, no pro forma balance sheet and no separate figures for the flat cap closures business; the stated cash sources of USD 5.9 billion exceed the stated cash uses of USD 2.3 billion to Silgan and USD 327.5 million to Trivium's sellers by about USD 3.27 billion, close to the USD 3.1 billion of Trivium debt, which is consistent with refinancing that debt but does not establish it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 19–20; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation A12

Silgan issued no notes or term loans in the first nine months of 2026. The last new issue was EUR 600.0 million of senior notes due 2031, sold at par on September 12, 2025 and used to repay euro revolving loans that had funded the March 15, 2025 repayment of EUR 650.0 million of senior notes. In 2026 Silgan prepaid USD 42.5 million of U.S. term loans on February 3, amended the Credit Agreement on March 6 to improve term loan pricing, and on March 31 repaid all USD 500.0 million of its 1.4% secured notes with revolving loans and cash, which released the subsidiary guarantees of the other three note series. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120, 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Silgan Holdings Inc (issuer slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway, run slgn-849869-2026-11-18-credit_snapshot-host. Scope: whether the five supplied SEC filings of the registrant (two annual and three quarterly reports) can support the requested Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work, and what the rest of the pathway would lack. No objective was stated, so the pathway's own question, whether to own this issuer, in which instrument and why, is the objective.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No upstream module output was supplied to this module; it is the first module of the run.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied filings support financial-statement, debt and business work through the third quarter of 2026, but not covenant, legal-ranking, rating or transaction conclusions, so creditors cannot yet test covenant headroom or claim priority from this source set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A material open item is the transaction announced on October 19, 2026, which would place the Metal Containers segment in a majority-owned partnership with its own secured debt; the quarterly report describes it in a single note, so the perimeter after closing and any pro forma leverage are not established. The executed credit agreement and indentures, agency ratings and dated market quotes are not supplied, and the filings print no covenant levels, so Legal & covenants work cannot run until the documents arrive. Annual figures are audited and interim figures are unaudited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No executed credit agreement, amendment or indenture is in the source set. The annual report lists them as exhibits and the first-quarter report lists the sixth amendment dated March 6, 2026, but the run settings declare no legal documents, so covenant definitions, baskets, guarantor and security terms and the call and change-of-control terms cannot be read from the governing documents. Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control and Recovery & fulcrum work would rest on filing summaries alone and cannot run until the documents are supplied. This is a material gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings name two financial covenants, Interest Coverage and Total Net Leverage, and state that the company is in compliance, but print no covenant level, no step-down and no reported ratio. Covenant headroom is therefore not established, and the credit agreement's own definition of Total Net Leverage is not available to compare with any leverage measure built from the statements. This is a material gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The announcement of October 19, 2026 is described only in one note to the third-quarter report: a partnership with an investment vehicle affiliated with funds managed by American Industrial Partners, the contribution of the Metal Containers segment and the food and beverage flat cap closures business, about USD 2.3 billion of cash to the company intended to retire existing debt, a 60% controlling interest for the company and 40% for the partner, about USD 1.0 billion of partner cash, about USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans and a USD 1.0 billion secured revolver at the partnership, and the proposed acquisition of Trivium Packaging B.V. for about USD 327.5 million in cash plus about USD 3.1 billion of assumed debt, expected to close in mid-2027 subject to regulatory approvals and works council consultation. No agreement, sources and uses, pro forma balance sheet, pro forma leverage or separate figures for the flat cap closures business are supplied, so the perimeter and pro forma net debt after closing are not established, and every figure in the filings is a reported pre-transaction figure that must not be blended with the announcement. This is a material gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Directors, executive compensation, beneficial ownership and director independence are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not in the source set; only the signature page names the directors and officers. Governance and ownership assessment in Business & governance is limited to what the business and risk sections state. This is a material gap for that work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The guarantor perimeter changed inside the period: the subsidiary guarantees of the three senior note series were released on March 31, 2026. Summarized obligor-group figures are printed only as of and for 2025 and 2024, the 2026 reports give none, and the exhibit naming the current subsidiary guarantors and issuers of guaranteed securities is listed but not supplied. Structural priority work cannot rely on the 2025 obligor-group figures for the current guarantor set. This is a material gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No agency credit rating, outlook or rating report appears in any of the five filings or in the run settings, so Ratings & triggers work would have nothing to start from. This is a minor gap for the requested work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No bond price, yield or spread on a dated trading day is supplied. The third-quarter report prints period-end fair values for the three senior note series, estimated from quoted market prices, which gives a quarter-end price level but not a trade date, yield or spread; Market-implied risk and Security selection work are limited to that. This is a minor gap for the requested work.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Silgan Holdings Inc (issuer slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership, governance, history and announced-transaction facts that matter to a creditor, from the five supplied filings of the registrant and the source readiness output; leverage, covenant levels, legal ranking and recovery are left to the modules that own them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplied upstream output: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 dea6590f16107f877923b231c0ec26ca6e7c92ecf169979faaaa0597ab3a987a.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Silgan is a scaled, contract-anchored packaging issuer, but the announced partnership would move its largest segment by sales into a separately financed structure that outside investors part-own, so creditors cannot yet size claim priority or leverage. Metal Containers produced 48.4% of 2025 net sales and 36.0% of adjusted EBIT, and Silgan would keep a 60% controlling interest and receive about USD 2.3 billion of cash that it intends to use to retire certain existing debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance is conventional for a listed company with no sponsor: the supplied filings document no related-party payments, dividends took 29.74% of 2025 net income and the USD 500.0 million buyback authorization was untouched through September 2026. The gap is control: who the larger holders are, and what the founders' stockholders agreement says, sit in documents that are not in the source set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is diversified across three packaging segments and anchored by contracts that pass raw-material cost through, which gives creditors more cash-flow visibility than a single-product packager would. Metal Containers was 48.4% of 2025 net sales, Dispensing and Specialty Closures 41.8% and Custom Containers 9.8%; about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year arrangements, metal costs pass through by contract and resin costs pass through with a lag in many cases. The other side is a thin metal margin: Metal Containers earned an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% in 2025 against 15.5% in Dispensing and Specialty Closures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nestlé is the one material customer concentration, and it is protected by contract rather than removed. Nestlé bought 14% of 2025 consolidated net sales and 13% in 2024 and 2023, and no other customer passed 10%; metal food containers sold to Nestlé were USD 799.8 million, or 12.3% of group sales, under long-term supply agreements that run through 2032 and price by formula. A loss or repricing would fall mainly on Metal Containers, the segment the announced partnership would hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Underlying 2026 operating momentum is weaker than the sales line suggests. Nine-month net sales rose 4.6%, mostly from cost pass-through and currency, while unit volumes fell in all three segments and adjusted EBIT was flat at USD 572.2 million against USD 572.6 million. An inventory program liquidated older LIFO layers and cut cost of goods sold by USD 34.0 million in the nine months, USD 26.8 million of it in the third quarter; if the whole benefit sits in adjusted EBIT, the measure would have been 6.01% below the prior-year nine months and 5.97% below the prior-year quarter without it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15–16, 18–20, 22–23; calculation A13; calculation A14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The announced perimeter takes the largest segment by sales, and a large share of earnings, out of the direct reach of Silgan's existing creditors. Metal Containers contributed 36.0% of 2025 adjusted EBIT and 38.60% in the first nine months of 2026, and the perimeter also includes a flat cap closures business whose size is not stated. Silgan would own 60% of the partnership and consolidate it, but the partnership's USD 4.9 billion of new senior secured term loans and USD 1.0 billion secured revolver would be secured by the partnership's assets only, and the other 40% would belong to an investment vehicle affiliated with American Industrial Partners that contributes about USD 1.0 billion of cash. Unless existing guarantees and share pledges continue to cover the contributed subsidiaries, which the note does not say, existing creditors of the parent would reach those assets only through the 60% interest, after the partnership's own lenders. The partnership would also buy Trivium, which the 2025 annual report names among the most significant metal container competitors, so the combination adds scale in the segment that already carries the largest customer concentration and depends on regulatory approval.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation A2; calculation A3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The senior notes now rest on the parent alone while the bank debt keeps subsidiary support. The U.S. subsidiaries' guarantees of the three unsecured senior note series, USD 1,849.38 million of principal and 40.54% of total debt at September 30, 2026, fell away automatically on March 31, 2026 when the secured 1.4% notes were repaid, and the filings print no replacement guarantor. The Credit Agreement, 57.51% of debt principal, stays guaranteed by the U.S. subsidiaries and a Dutch borrower subsidiary and is supported by pledges of subsidiary shares, so noteholders sit behind subsidiary-level claims, and the partnership's secured lenders would add another layer ahead of them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management states that it uses leverage to fund growth and shareholder returns, and the 2024 to 2026 record matches that policy. Weener Packaging cost USD 921.6 million net of cash acquired in October 2024 and was financed with euro loans and cash; dividends have risen every year since 2004; cash returned through dividends and repurchases was 80.65% of net income in 2023, 33.06% in 2024, 55.71% in 2025 and 30.82% in the first nine months of 2026; interest and other debt expense absorbed 31.7% of 2025 income before interest and taxes. The planned USD 2.3 billion debt retirement would be creditor-supportive if completed, but the same announcement adds about USD 3.1 billion of Trivium debt to be assumed, so the net effect on consolidated debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10, 55, 59–60, 75, 109; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16; calculation A8; calculation A9; calculation A12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Working capital leans on bank-run programs, which is funding that is not counted as debt. Customer-based supply chain finance programs covered about 16% of net sales in 2025 and 2024 and improved days sales outstanding by about 28 days, and supplier invoices in the supplier program were USD 482.0 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 385.8 million a year earlier, up 24.94%. If the programs ended, net working capital would rise and the revolver would fund it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance is conventional and the audit record is clean, but the control picture is incomplete. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named; the company had 20 holders of record at January 31, 2026; the board is classified and fixed at seven seats subject to a temporary increase, while nine directors signed the annual report; the chair and the chief executive are different people; the auditor has served since 1987 and gave unqualified opinions, including on internal control; and no restatement, waiver or going-concern statement appears. Director independence, compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the 2022 founders' stockholders agreement is listed but not supplied, so the sponsor and governance risk read is medium and provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the announced transaction, if completed as described, would pay down about half of the group's debt: the USD 2.3 billion cash distribution equals 50.42% of total debt principal at September 30, 2026, and Silgan would keep control and full consolidation of the segment. The operating base also has a resilient record: multi-year contracts covered about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales, the USD 50 million cost program was completed with about USD 20 million of savings in 2024 and about USD 30 million in 2025, adjusted EBIT rose to USD 723.3 million in 2025 from USD 658.2 million, and the supplied filings show no covenant waiver, restatement, related-party payment or exchange offer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Executed agreements and a pro forma capital structure would settle the largest open question: which debt is retired, whether the Trivium debt is refinanced or stays in place, and whether the partnership's lenders have any recourse to Silgan. Which instruments are retired decides whether the remaining parent claims are mostly secured bank debt or unsecured notes. Evidence of a large founder or fund holder, or terms in the 2022 stockholders agreement that bind the board, would move the governance read from conventional to influenced. A debt-funded dividend or repurchase after the transaction, loss or repricing of the Nestlé agreement, or a second year of volume declines without pass-through offsets would move the view the other way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The October 2026 announcement is described in one note with no executed agreements, sources and uses or pro forma balance sheet, so the conclusions on claim priority, perimeter and debt after closing are directional and rest on pre-transaction figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement, the Schedule 13G holder names and the 2022 founders' stockholders agreement are not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists rests on the absence of a named sponsor and would change if a founder or fund holds a large block.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Only segment sales, adjusted EBIT, depreciation, assets and capital expenditure are printed by segment, so the share of group cash flow that would sit in the partnership is approximated by its adjusted EBIT share and could differ materially.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer contracts are not supplied, so the revenue durability conclusion rests on management's statements of contract coverage and the Nestlé end date, and renewal, termination or volume commitments could be weaker than stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Statements that the company is a leader or has more than half of the U.S. metal food container market are management's and are not tested against independent market data, so the competitive position conclusion is management's view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The nine-month 2026 figures are unaudited and the inventory benefit is stated only for the group, so the underlying earnings estimate changes if part of that benefit sits outside adjusted EBIT.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On October 19, 2026 Silgan announced agreements to create a partnership, Silgan MCC, with an investment vehicle affiliated with funds managed by American Industrial Partners. Silgan would contribute its Metal Containers segment and its food and beverage flat cap closures business and would receive about USD 2.3 billion of cash, which it intends to use to retire certain existing debt, and a 60% controlling ownership interest; the investment vehicle would contribute about USD 1.0 billion of cash for 40%. The partnership would have an independent balance sheet that is fully consolidated into Silgan's statements and would be financed by about USD 4.9 billion of new senior secured term loans and a new senior secured revolving facility of USD 1.0 billion, which the company describes as fully committed and secured by assets of the partnership only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The partnership would also acquire Trivium Packaging B.V., a Netherlands supplier of metal packaging, for a cash payment of about USD 327.5 million and the assumption of about USD 3.1 billion of Trivium's debt. Trivium is one of the competitors that the 2025 annual report names among the most significant in metal containers. Closing is expected in mid-2027 and is subject to regulatory approvals, works council consultation and customary conditions. Costs attributed to announced acquisitions were USD 10.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, against USD 1.1 million in the first nine months of 2025, and adjusted EBIT excludes them; the filing does not tie them to a named transaction. The note gives no agreement terms, no sources and uses, no pro forma balance sheet and no separate figures for the flat cap closures business; the stated cash sources of USD 5.9 billion exceed the stated cash uses of USD 2.3 billion to Silgan and USD 327.5 million to Trivium's sellers by about USD 3.27 billion, close to the USD 3.1 billion of Trivium debt, which is consistent with refinancing that debt but does not establish it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Silgan issued no notes or term loans in the first nine months of 2026. The last new issue was EUR 600.0 million of senior notes due 2031, sold at par on September 12, 2025 and used to repay euro revolving loans that had funded the March 15, 2025 repayment of EUR 650.0 million of senior notes. In 2026 Silgan prepaid USD 42.5 million of U.S. term loans on February 3, amended the Credit Agreement on March 6 to improve term loan pricing, and on March 31 repaid all USD 500.0 million of its 1.4% secured notes with revolving loans and cash, which released the subsidiary guarantees of the other three note series.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by a stated policy of using leverage for growth and shareholder returns and by the unquantified Silgan MCC transaction, because that policy allows debt to rise again after any paydown and the transaction changes claim ranking, which implies refinancing and monitoring exposure. Countervailing evidence is the record of early refinancing, no waivers, no liability management exchange and a conventional board with a separate chair. Further analysis requires the transaction agreements, the proxy statement and the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The announcement of October 19, 2026 is described in a single note, so the executed agreements, sources and uses, the debt to be retired, whether the Trivium debt stays in place, any recourse to Silgan, the partner's governance rights and the size of the flat cap closures business are all missing. The stated cash sources exceed the stated cash uses by about USD 3.27 billion, which is close to the Trivium debt but is not explained. This is a material gap for the corporate structure and claim priority conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership detail is missing. The proxy statement, the names of holders of 10% or more, director and officer ownership and the 2022 founders' stockholders agreement are not in the source set, so the conclusion that the company has no controlling holder rests on the absence of a named sponsor. This is a material gap for the governance read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer contracts, including the Nestlé agreements that run through 2032, are not supplied, so price formulas, termination rights and volume commitments cannot be read. This is a minor gap for the revenue durability conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weener Packaging results are not shown separately after the October 2024 acquisition, so its contribution to the 17.5% growth in dispensing and specialty closures sales in 2025 cannot be separated from organic growth. This is a minor gap for the acquisition integration evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ownership percentages of the three joint ventures and the lists of subsidiaries and guarantors after the March 31, 2026 release are exhibits that are not supplied. This is a minor gap for the ownership map.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No agency credit rating or outlook is stated in any supplied filing or in the run settings. This is a minor gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Segment-level debt, cash flow and working capital are not printed, so the cash flow that would sit in the partnership is approximated by adjusted EBIT share only. This is a minor gap for the perimeter conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company's statements that it is a leader in each business and holds more than half of the U.S. metal food container market are not tested against independent market data, and the estimate of the market still served by self-manufacturers moved from about 6% in the 2024 annual report to about 7% in the 2025 annual report. This is a minor gap for the competitive position conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Silgan Holdings Inc (issuer slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit profile of the registrant from the five supplied filings and the earlier outputs of this run, covering business durability, cash conversion, leverage, liquidity, refinancing capacity and financial policy; legal ranking, covenant capacity, recovery and relative value are left to the modules that own them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplied upstream outputs: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 dea6590f16107f877923b231c0ec26ca6e7c92ecf169979faaaa0597ab3a987a; Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 b7a568c70f4b6a8ec9738cf7ce2fec91b44d5085aa4bc7ba31a0b20aef8a3998; Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 5304f642cc07310ee6887b15df3169eeb6f5cd6fe4454c4e0e34415568e84872.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Silgan's fundamental credit profile is adequate: contract-backed cash flows and steady free cash flow support the debt, but flat 2026 earnings, seasonal net leverage of 4.67x and an unquantified October 2026 transaction leave creditors with less cushion than year-end figures suggest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow of about USD 423 million covered 2025 dividends and buybacks 2.63 times, and liquidity of about USD 991 million at September 30, 2026 exceeds the roughly USD 600 million seasonal need the company cites. Net leverage was 3.56x at year-end 2025; the pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement on net debt and net leverage is not established. About 60.14% of principal falls due in 2028 and 2030, so how the transaction retires debt will shape the refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 27; calculation D3; calculation D4; calculation D7; calculation D9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business supports the debt through contract-backed, cost-pass-through earnings rather than growth. Reported EBITDA margins stayed between 13.51% and 14.34% from 2023 to 2025 even though EBITDA fell 7.88% in 2024; about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year contracts that pass metal cost through, while resin cost passes through with a lag. The price is thin metal margins, an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% in 2025, and one concentration, Nestlé at 14% of 2025 net sales under agreements that run through 2032.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17, 21–25, 66–68; calculation D1; calculation D2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow covers distributions but has not reduced debt. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was about USD 423 million in 2025, 46.10% of reported EBITDA, and covered dividends and buybacks 2.63 times; yet net debt fell only USD 47.81 million and total debt rose, so the improvement in leverage came from EBITDA growth, not repayment. Free cash flow after shareholder returns was about USD 262 million, a pace that would not shrink net debt quickly against a seasonal swing of the size seen in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104; calculation D3; calculation D4; calculation D5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is elevated at the seasonal peak and the 2026 earnings trend does not help. Net debt over reported EBITDA was 3.56x at year-end 2025, and the pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement on that figure is not established; it was 4.67x at September 30, 2026 on last-twelve-months EBITDA, with total debt at 5.03x. Last-twelve-months EBITDA of about USD 904 million is 1.44% below 2025, and it would be a further 3.76% lower, with net leverage at 4.85x, without the USD 34.0 million inventory benefit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15, 18–20; calculation D2; calculation D6; calculation D10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate in aggregate but thinnest in early summer, and two maturity years concentrate the refinancing test. Cash plus revolver availability was about USD 991 million at September 30, 2026 but about USD 754 million at June 30, when revolver availability of USD 402.4 million was below the USD 600 million seasonal need; the USD 1,500.0 million revolver matures in November 2029. At December 31, 2025, 31.89% of principal fell due in 2028 and 28.25% in 2030, together 60.14%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73, 114; calculation D7; calculation D9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The October 2026 transaction is the swing factor for claim priority and leverage, and the filings do not let a creditor size it. The USD 2.3 billion distribution equals 50.42% of total debt principal at September 30, 2026, 124.37% of the unsecured senior notes and 87.66% of Credit Agreement debt, so which instruments are retired decides whether the remaining parent claims are mostly secured bank debt or mostly unsecured notes; the partnership's USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans rank on its own assets only, and the Trivium acquisition is expected to close in mid-2027, ahead of the 2028 note maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Funding that does not show as debt deepens reliance on banks. Supplier invoices in the supply chain finance program were USD 482.0 million at September 30, 2026, up 24.94% in a year and equal to 10.60% of total debt, and customer programs covered about 16% of net sales; the bank can end the supplier program on short notice, which would turn payables into revolver draws at the point of seasonal peak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 27–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are a moderate risk rather than a decisive one. Dividends took 29.74% of 2025 net income and the USD 500.0 million buyback authorization was unused in the first nine months of 2026, but management states that it uses leverage to fund growth and shareholder returns, interest and other debt expense absorbed 31.7% of 2025 income before interest and taxes, and ownership detail sits in documents that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that net debt at September 30, 2026 was about USD 335 million, 7.35%, below the same date a year earlier, last-twelve-months EBITDA covered cash interest 5.24x, the revolver runs to November 2029, and Silgan sold EUR 600.0 million of notes at par in September 2025. The announced distribution would also retire about half of total debt principal if applied as intended, and the 2024 pack shortfall showed that a weak packing year cut earnings but raised operating cash flow, partly because inventory built less.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; calculation D11; calculation D12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Year-end 2026 net leverage at or below the 3.56x of year-end 2025, a level whose pro forma effect from the October 19, 2026 announcement is not established, a pro forma capital structure that shows net leverage below that level after closing, early refinancing of the 2028 notes and a return of unit volume growth would improve the view. Year-end 2026 net leverage above the 4.67x of September 30, 2026, revolver availability below the USD 600 million seasonal need at the 2027 low, a distribution that retires secured bank debt while leaving the notes behind new secured debt, or a revolver-funded buyback would worsen it. Covenant levels, which would settle the headroom question, are not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 27; calculation D7; calculation D12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels and the credit agreement's own definition of leverage are not printed, so the conclusion that leverage and liquidity are adequate rests on trend and cash cover and cannot be tested against headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, dated bond quote or peer figure is supplied, so the adequate reading is an absolute view built on the issuer's own history, not a ranking against sector peers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is calculated as income before interest and taxes plus depreciation and amortization, after restructuring and acquisition costs and including the inventory benefit, because the company states no EBITDA, so every leverage ratio moves with that choice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma net debt, leverage and the instruments to be retired are not stated, so the refinancing and leverage conclusions describe the pre-transaction group only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity ladder is printed only at December 31, 2025 and predates the March 2026 repayment and prepayment, and no year-end 2026 estimate exists, so the maturity concentration is an approximation and the outlook and downside are qualitative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is contract-backed earnings. About 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year supply arrangements that pass metal cost through, and a majority of dispensing and custom container sales do too, so reported EBITDA margins held between 13.51% and 14.34% across 2023 to 2025. That gives creditors earnings that bend rather than break when input costs move, with resin cost recovery lagging as the exception.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17, 21–22, 58–59; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is cash conversion. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was about USD 423 million in 2025, 46.10% of reported EBITDA, which covered dividends and buybacks 2.63 times and left about USD 262 million to reduce debt or fund acquisitions. Operating cash flow is struck after cash interest of about USD 185 million, so that free cash flow is cash left after servicing the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D3; calculation D4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is a record of early and orderly refinancing. The Credit Agreement was extended to November 2029 for the revolver and November 2030 for term loans in November 2024, EUR 600.0 million of notes were sold at par in September 2025, and the USD 500.0 million secured notes were repaid in March 2026 ahead of their April maturity; no waiver, exchange offer or covenant breach appears in the filings. That lowers the risk that a market window decides the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is delivery on cost. The USD 50 million cost program was completed, with about USD 20 million of savings in 2024 and about USD 30 million in 2025, which supported the rise in 2025 adjusted EBIT to USD 723.3 million from USD 658.2 million and gives management a lever if volumes soften.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth strength is a conventional governance and audit record, with unqualified opinions, effective internal control and a payout of 29.74% of 2025 net income, which keeps shareholder claims on cash moderate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is that the October 2026 transaction leaves claim priority, perimeter and leverage open. The largest segment by sales would sit in a partnership that is 40% owned by an outside investor and financed by USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans on its own assets, and the effect on consolidated net debt and net leverage is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is elevated and seasonal leverage with flat 2026 earnings. Net debt over reported EBITDA reached 4.67x at September 30, 2026 against 3.56x at year-end 2025, for which the pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement is not established, unit volumes fell in all segments over the nine months, and adjusted EBIT was flat only because currency, mix in custom containers, manufacturing efficiencies and an inventory benefit offset lower volumes and a less favorable mix elsewhere.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15, 18–20; calculation D6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is a concentrated maturity profile. At December 31, 2025, 31.89% of principal fell due in 2028 and 28.25% in 2030, so two refinancing windows carry most of the principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is thin metal margins and one large customer. Metal Containers earned an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% and Nestlé was 14% of net sales, so a small cost lag or a repricing moves group earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is reliance on bank-run funding. Supplier finance invoices of USD 482.0 million and customer receivable programs covering about 16% of net sales move cash forward, and the seasonal borrowing that follows is carried on one revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Silgan is a listed holding company that makes dispensing systems and specialty closures, steel and aluminum food containers and custom plastic containers through three segments, with about USD 6.5 billion of 2025 net sales and 32% of sales from foreign operations. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named; ownership detail and the founders' stockholders agreement are not supplied, so financial policy is set by a classified board and management who state that they use leverage for growth. Creditors benefit from the simple perimeter of one consolidated registrant but must read subsidiary-level claims, because the senior notes lost their subsidiary guarantees on March 31, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable rather than growing. About 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales are under multi-year arrangements, Nestlé supplies 14% of group sales under agreements through 2032, metal cans are sold within about 300 miles of the plant, and customers may seek competing offers during a term, which Silgan can match at a lower price. Over the nine months of 2026 net sales rose 4.59% through cost pass-through and currency while unit volumes fell, so revenue visibility is about price pass-through, not volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against input cost over a year because metal cost passes through by contract, but not within a quarter: the third quarter of 2026 showed a delayed pass-through of freight and manufacturing inflation, a less favorable mix and lower volumes. Fixed cost absorption is the sensitive point, as in 2024 when a large pack customer and severe weather cut the fruit and vegetable pack and Metal Containers adjusted EBIT fell USD 39.98 million, 14.16%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is steady, with capital expenditure of about USD 307 million in 2025 and about USD 310 million expected for 2026, restructuring cash costs of USD 26.1 million in 2025 and USD 43.7 million in the first nine months of 2026, and cash taxes of about USD 150 million expected for 2026. Operating cash flow is negative in the first nine months because of the seasonal build, USD 646.363 million in 2026, which the revolver finances, so debt peaks in the summer and unwinds by year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high and price-sensitive: the annual report names several large metal container and closure competitors, says Silgan competes on price, quality and service, and notes that customers may self-manufacture, which about 7% of the U.S. metal food container market still does. Buyer power is high because a small number of large food and consumer goods customers hold multi-year contracts with competitive-proposal rights; supplier power is moderate because steel, aluminum and resin come from a limited number of suppliers, offset by pass-through clauses. The threat of new entrants is limited by plant proximity, with metal cans sold mostly within about 300 miles, and substitution by plastic, glass, paper and composite packaging is real outside high-temperature and long-shelf-life food uses. For creditors this means pricing power is limited and earnings depend on volume, mix and contract terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: External factors are material only where they hit pass-through or cost: steel and aluminum tariffs and quotas complicate cost recovery, bisphenol and PFAS rules have forced or may force product changes, natural gas disruption affects the European plants, about 32% of sales are earned abroad against euro debt, and a one percentage point rate move changed 2025 interest expense by about USD 15.7 million. Other political and social factors are not a primary credit driver on the evidence supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are contract-backed pass-through earnings, cash conversion and refinancing record; the weaknesses are seasonal leverage, thin metal margins, customer concentration and a transaction that is not yet sized; the opportunities are pet food and dispensing volume growth, where management points, and use of the unused buyback and distribution proceeds for debt reduction; the threats are a repeat of a short fruit and vegetable pack, delayed cost pass-through and a debt-funded use of capital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and diversification are supports: a group of about USD 6.5 billion of sales across three segments, with the largest customer at 14%. Competitive advantage is partial, resting on proximity, contracts and scale rather than pricing power. Cost and capex flexibility is moderate: capital expenditure near USD 310 million a year is not easily cut, though the cost program and plant closures show a lever. Margin stability is good on the three-year record and weaker on the 2026 volume trend. Free cash flow is stable in the annual figure and negative in the seasonal quarters. Access to capital markets has been shown by the September 2025 note sale at par, with no rating supplied. Liquidity is adequate in aggregate and thin in early summer. Financial policy is leverage-for-growth with moderate payouts. The trend is flat: earnings are level, debt is seasonally high, and the transaction adds uncertainty; the key missing datapoints are covenant levels, a rating, pro forma figures and customer contract terms.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 75, 119–120; calculation D3; calculation D7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months management expected higher volumes in dispensing and specialty closures and in metal containers for 2026 and flat custom container volumes, but over nine months of 2026 unit volumes were about 2% lower in dispensing and specialty closures, about 1% lower in metal containers and about 8% lower in custom containers, so the company's own expectation has not been met so far. Tailwinds are pet food growth, prescription dispensing and fragrance volumes, the Europe closure savings and lower interest expense; headwinds are weak beverage closure demand, soup volumes, delayed cost pass-through, tariffs and a higher effective tax rate. Over three to five years the question is whether volume recovery and cost savings, not pass-through pricing, drive earnings, and how the partnership changes the group's debt and ownership.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A realistic downside starts with a short fruit and vegetable pack combined with weaker pet food and beverage closure volumes in 2027, the pattern of 2024 when severe weather and a large customer's cut in pack plans lowered fixed cost absorption in Metal Containers and group reported EBITDA fell 7.88%. The first operational break is lower plant utilization and delayed pass-through of freight and resin cost; the financial effect is lower EBITDA: applying the 2024 fall to 2025 EBITDA gives about USD 845 million and net leverage of 3.87x on year-end 2025 net debt, and applying it to last-twelve-months EBITDA gives about USD 833 million, net leverage of 5.07x on September 2026 seasonal net debt and cash interest cover near 4.83x. Because a short pack also builds less inventory, operating cash flow rose in 2024 and liquidity was protected, so the strain falls on leverage and refinancing, not on liquidity, as the 2028 notes approach and while the partnership's debt is consolidated. Management levers are the cost program, capital expenditure near USD 310 million, the unused buyback and the USD 2.3 billion distribution. Liquidity appears sufficient to avoid distress; the primary downside path is volume and pass-through pressure that lifts leverage while the 2028 maturities and the transaction compete for the same refinancing window. The 2024 decline also included restructuring and acquisition costs, so it is a bound for an adverse year, not a forecast, and none of these ratios includes the October 19, 2026 announcement, whose pro forma effect on net debt and net leverage is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Silgan presents an adequate business profile supported by contract-backed pass-through earnings, steady free cash flow and a record of early refinancing, but credit quality is constrained by seasonal net leverage of 4.67x, flat 2026 earnings, a concentrated 2028 and 2030 maturity profile and a transaction that leaves claim priority open. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because 2025 free cash flow covered distributions 2.63 times and margins held through the 2024 shock. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how the USD 2.3 billion distribution is applied, on market access in 2027 and on the bank group's appetite for the revolver to 2029. The primary downside path is volume and pass-through pressure that lifts leverage while the 2028 maturities and the transaction compete for the same refinancing window. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the executed credit agreement, pro forma net debt and leverage, a rating and customer contract terms. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: leverage and claim priority after the transaction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The executed credit agreement, its amendments and the indentures are not supplied and the filings print no covenant level, step-down or reported ratio, so headroom, restricted payment capacity and the credit agreement's definition of leverage cannot be read. This is a material gap for the leverage and liquidity conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The October 19, 2026 announcement gives no sources and uses, pro forma balance sheet, pro forma net debt or leverage, or list of the debt to be retired, and the stated cash sources exceed the stated cash uses by about USD 3.27 billion, close to the Trivium debt to be assumed. This is a material gap for the refinancing, leverage and claim ranking conclusions.

fields.value: Customer contract terms, including the Nestlé agreements, are not supplied. This is a minor gap for revenue durability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Segment-level debt, cash flow and working capital are not printed, so the cash flow of the segment proposed for the partnership is approximated by adjusted EBIT. This is a minor gap for the transaction conclusion.

fields.value: The supplied analysis and filings give no bridge from 2025 free cash flow to the change in net debt and do not quantify translation of euro debt, so why net debt fell only USD 47.81 million against free cash flow after shareholder returns of about USD 262 million is not established. This is a minor gap for the cash conversion conclusion.
